To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate quantum coherent coupling between optical photons, and a micromechanically oscillating membrane.
we have achieved coherent coupling between an optical cavity mode and a micromechanically oscillating mirror, and that this coherent coupling is used to cool the mirror to the ground state.

we have demonstrated the coherent coupling between optical photons (in a cavity) and mechanical oscillators (in the cavity), and have used this coupling to coherently control the quantum state of the oscillator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction between light and mechanical motion in a high-finesse optical cavity.
the development and use of quantum mechanical oscillators.
the development and use of optomechanical systems to control and probe quantum states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have achieved quantum coherent coupling of optical fields to micromechanical motion.
quantum coherent coupling between optical photons in a high finesse optical resonator and a mechanical oscillator has been achieved.
we demonstrate the quantum coherent coupling between a mechanical oscillator and a light field, and the cooling of the mechanical oscillator to a mean phonon number below 2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the coupling of the optical field and the mechanical motion of the oscillator is so strong that it can exchange a single quantum of motion with the optical field.
we have achieved a coherent coupling between a microwave and an optical field, which is a prerequisite for the implementation of quantum communication between these frequency regimes.
we have achieved quantum-coherent coupling in an optomechanical device at room temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that

quantum-coherent coupling can be achieved between optical photons and mechanical oscillators at room temperature, which opens up the possibility of using mechanical oscillators as transducers between microwave and optical quantum systems.
we have achieved the quantum coherent coupling of optical fields and micromechanical motion in a system that operates at ambient temperature, with no cryogenic cooling or other special conditions.
the quantum coherent coupling between optical and micromechanical degrees of freedom has now been demonstrated.
